name: Atlanta stacked-ribbon optical cable
summary: Bell Laboratories packaged optical fibers in stacked adhesive-backed ribbons for group handling and splicing in the Atlanta Fiber System Experiment.
description: The cable stacked twelve ribbons of twelve Western Electric graded-index glass fibers inside a protective sheath. Each ribbon held its fibers in a line so workers could prepare and join multiple fibers together.
tier_reason: This record covers the particular Bell Laboratories Atlanta cable configuration demonstrated in 1976.

date.basis: Figure 5 of the Chicago project report labels the measured Atlanta cable 1975.

events.statement: Bell Laboratories made a twelve-ribbon optical cable for the Atlanta experiment in 1975.
events.scope: The cable assembled for the Atlanta Fiber System Experiment. The comparison labels the cable year. The fabrication day is unrecorded.

evidence.locator: Printed pp. 1745–1747 / PDF pp. 29–31, §§II–III and Figs. 1–2
evidence.supports: The fabrication report describes the Atlanta experiment cable as a stack of twelve ribbons with twelve fibers per ribbon, selected to facilitate group splicing.
The project team's loss comparison labels the Atlanta experimental cable 1975 and the Chicago project cables 1976.

date.label: 13 January 1976
date.basis: The experiment’s overview dates the full-system transmission test to this day.

events.statement: The Atlanta Fiber System Experiment sent 44.7 Mb/s test signals over a complete optical system fitted with the stacked-ribbon cable.
events.place_note: Joint Bell Laboratories and Western Electric facility in the Atlanta area, Georgia.
events.scope: Simulated telephone plant around the Atlanta research and manufacturing facility.
events.caveats: The field-like ducts belonged to an experimental facility. The twelve nominal fibers per ribbon give 144 positions, and manufacturing breaks reduced the number of transmitting fibers.

evidence.locator: Printed p. 1717 / PDF p. 1, opening and experiment objectives
evidence.supports: The experiment transmitted at 44.7 Mb/s over the complete system on 13 January 1976 under simulated plant conditions.

earliest_record.rationale: The dated 1975 cable in the engineering comparison is an earlier witness to the manufactured configuration than the dated 1976 system test.

caveats: The record concerns the specific adhesive-sandwich stack adopted for Atlanta. The engineers cite earlier ribbon concepts and earlier work on group splicing.

research.note: Buckler, Santana and Saunders identify the cable and manufacturing practice. Jacobs dates its tested system and Schwartz and colleagues date the cable comparison. The scope-based tier is an editorial classification.
